## 固定收益市場主線

10月21日，美國短天期公債殖利率上升，30年期公債則延續漲勢，殖利率曲線進一步趨平。科技業獲利重新提振市場信心，但通膨壓力仍在：2年期殖利率上升2.99個基點至4.806%，10年期上升1.05個基點至5.119%，30年期下降1.09個基點至5.4089%。10年期實質殖利率幾乎不變，名目殖利率的小幅上升來自通膨補償增加。

SpaceX財報帶動市場重拾對AI需求的信心，科技股反彈，但投資人評估支應成長所需的舉債規模，其債券反而走弱。這種股債分歧是當日行情的核心：營運改善足以支撐股價，卻未解決債權人必須承接多少新增債務的問題。能源則從另一方向施壓。船舶持續遇襲，伊朗也為恢復外交談判提出條件，布蘭特原油收在每桶$110以上。

最新房貸數據顯示，美國借款成本小幅下降仍未帶動購屋需求。海外方面，英國通膨升幅超出預期，政府舉債也高於預測；法國公債殖利率與對德利差雙雙觸及新的關卡。南非則形成對照，預算案削減每週發債規模並推進新的財政框架，帶動債市上漲。這些市場各自面臨融資條件的變化，並非同步回應美債的溫和波動。

## 美債曲線趨平，能源壓力仍未消退

美國正常交易時段風險偏好回升，短中天期公債殖利率也走高。標普500指數上漲0.58%，那斯達克100指數上漲1.13%，半導體股上漲1.97%。市場近期重新評估AI投資後，SpaceX財報與美超微強勁的初步業績，讓投資人對當前科技需求恢復信心。VIX下降3.64%至16.68。

長天期公債表現仍優於短端。5年期殖利率上升2.15個基點至4.9506%；2年期與30年期殖利率反向變動，使2年與30年期利差收窄4.08個基點至60.29個基點，2年與10年期利差也收窄1.94個基點至31.3個基點。科技股反彈的同時，曲線進一步趨平，近期長天期債券的漲勢並未全面逆轉。

從週線看，債市漲勢依然集中在長端：10年期與30年期殖利率一週分別下降6.64與11.42個基點，2年期卻上升0.85個基點。不過，10年期與30年期殖利率一個月來仍分別上升12.2與8.19個基點。近期長端回穩只收復了部分失地，尚未消除融資成本的升幅。

10年期實質殖利率微降0.09個基點至2.7494%，損益兩平通膨率則上升1.14個基點至2.3696%，顯示名目殖利率上揚來自通膨補償，而非實質利率重新承受上行壓力。一週以來，實質殖利率下降7.54個基點，損益兩平通膨率仍增加0.9個基點；長天期公債改善，通膨定價卻未隨之降溫。

能源提供了具體原因。布蘭特原油上漲1.16%，收在每桶$110.05，一週與一個月漲幅分別達3.76%與10.84%；西德州原油上漲0.24%，收在$98.05。較早交易時段，伊朗國營媒體報導，一艘超級油輪在荷姆茲海峽觸雷。船舶接連遇襲，持續干擾這條水道的通行。

伊朗外交部長Abbas Araghchi表示，只要華府解除海上封鎖，並展現認真推動外交的承諾，伊朗願意就結束戰爭展開談判。他也呼籲回到6月的《伊斯蘭馬巴德諒解備忘錄》；該備忘錄將重開海峽，與美國結束封鎖、解凍伊朗石油資金及解除制裁相互連結。

美國庫存數據則呈現原油與汽油減幅大於預期、蒸餾油反而增加的分歧。截至10月16日當週，EIA原油庫存減少306.1萬桶，經濟學家原估減少80萬桶，前值為減少855.7萬桶。汽油庫存減少295.2萬桶，預估減少40萬桶，前一週則增加351.8萬桶。蒸餾油庫存增加167.5萬桶，原估減少120萬桶，前值為減少252.7萬桶。原油與汽油庫存收緊，但成品油各項庫存變化並不一致。

摩根士丹利另預期，即使戰爭造成的干擾緩解，異常密集的煉油廠歲修仍將限制供應，油品市場將持續吃緊至2027年中。高盛估計，全球原油運輸成本約為一年前的7倍。這些判斷關注實體供應壓力的持續時間與成本，影響不止於眼前的外交消息。

美國房市則再度顯示高利率已在抑制需求。截至10月16日當週，美國抵押貸款銀行協會的30年期固定房貸合約利率下降9個基點至7.41%，為8月初以來首次下降，但仍較一年前高出逾1個百分點。購屋貸款申請減少7.3%，連續第七週下滑，降至2025年1月初以來最低。

整體房貸申請繼前一週下降2.7%後，再減少5.3%；房貸市場指數由199.2降至188.6，購屋指數由139.3降至129.2。轉貸申請連續第九週走弱，指數由513.5降至503.1，為去年年初以來最低。房貸利率的小幅改善，仍不足以止住融資需求惡化。

美國財政部20年期公債標售得標殖利率為5.469%，高於前次的5.420%。當日30年期殖利率下跌，這場標售卻呈現長天期實際融資成本上升。除了成本，政府債券需求的組成變化也愈來愈受關注。

Bloomberg週三刊出的分析指出，民間投資人持有約70%的聯邦債務，接近1990年以來最高占比。避險基金於2025年底持有約8.5%的流通美債，金額約$2.7兆；2012至2025年間，其部位已增為原來的4倍。巴克萊策略師Anshul Pradhan認為，相較於有大量不敏感於價格的官方買盤支撐的市場，倚賴可自主決定進出的民間資金，可能必須提供更大的價格讓利。

Bloomberg Economics估計，聯準會與外國官方持有量下降，一度使期限溢價增加約105個基點。Milliman數據另顯示，9月企業退休基金資產約為履行負債所需的114%，2020年7月則為82%。NISA的Stephen Douglass指出，已凍結或關閉的確定給付退休計畫，不再累積新的遠期負債，因此長期資產負債配對需求的成長受到限制。

槓桿買方可以吸收供給，但融資條件至關重要。TS Lombard的Steven Blitz表示，附買回利率若急升，可能迫使相對價值交易平倉。同篇報導也指出，美債基差交易近幾個月已縮小。

## AI財報轉強，債權人仍聚焦融資需求

SpaceX財報雖有助科技股上漲，其債券週三卻下跌。截至紐約時間下午12時35分，2046年到期、票息6.6%的債券利差擴大9個基點至264個基點。ICE Data Services數據顯示，5年期信用違約交換報價一度上升0.8個基點，至每年約232.6個基點，逆轉稍早收窄的走勢。

市場新近關注的是管理層對投資計畫的說明。財務長Bret Johnsen在週二財報電話會議表示，公司正積極投入Super Intelligence運算、Starlink寬頻及行動服務；他強調維持投資等級評等的意向，同時說明正與數個債務資金來源洽談，以支應成長。營運擴張幅度確實可觀，Super Intelligence在9月當季營收達$75.6億，超過一年前的9倍。

這也解釋了股債反應為何不同：營收上升可以強化股票投資人支持擴張的理由，但為擴張融資，也會增加債權人預期必須承接的供給。SpaceX原已洽談$400億晶片融資，是Johnsen這次談話的直接背景。即使獲利改善，債市仍將焦點放在未來資金需求。

其他公司的營運挫折，則顯示專案預期現金流可能迅速改變。澳洲Nextdc週三股價重挫42%，此前公司將獲利指引下修逾三分之一，並表示正考慮援引不可抗力條款的可能方案。社區反對使其墨爾本大型專案的供電延後。知情人士表示，新加坡DayOne Data Centers正考慮將美國IPO延至市場回穩，或將發行規模縮至$25億至$30億，約為最初目標的一半。

兩者處於不同融資階段：Nextdc面臨既有專案延後通電，DayOne則重新考慮股權募資的時點與規模。對必須先投入建設、才能提供可用運算容量的產業而言，兩者都重要。貝萊德執行長Larry Fink週三從供給面提出另一觀點，認為資料中心建設延誤可能使運算成本居高不下，威脅成長；加快建設則可能降低成本。

Apollo的Torsten Slok本週研究報告對需求無上限的假設提出質疑。他指出，運算token支出放緩，顯示買方即使面對小幅價格變化也相當敏感，願意減少用量或尋找更便宜的替代方案。他也認為，資本報酬率下降正擠壓資料中心供應商。除了業者的融資與建設限制，他的判斷也把付費使用的經濟效益納入考量。

更廣泛的高收益債市場，取得融資的代價已提高，即使週三美國高收益債利差仍小幅收窄。Bloomberg最新彙總顯示，本月美國與歐洲至少7家公司延後發債，總額超過$50億，是今年最集中的延後發行潮。美國垃圾債10月至今發行約$70億，9月為$510億。B級債券殖利率週二升至8.39%，創18個月新高；CCC級殖利率達15.7%，為4年高點。

融資放緩不只出現在原已陷入困境的AI公司。Circet延後一筆原擬在歐元及美元市場進行的€30億再融資。ICG的David Saitowitz指出，光是基準利率就足以讓信用市場活動降溫；穆迪的John Puchalla同樣強調，高槓桿借款人承受額外償債負擔。週三次級市場高收益債利差溫和收窄，與初級市場明顯收緊的環境同時存在。

貝萊德週三公布的季度固定收益展望，則指出殖利率上升帶來的另一面。該公司表示，現在可建立殖利率超過7%、存續期間低於3年、平均評等A-的分散投資組合。其歐洲、中東與非洲地區全球固定收益主管James Turner強調，較高的利息收入有助抵禦利率上升或利差擴大。歐元投資等級公司債今年報酬約為負0.5%，期間ECB已升息兩次，利差也較最窄水準擴大逾20個基點；相較之下，2022年虧損超過13%。

貝萊德認為，部分公用事業、電信與能源公司的混合資本債，以及部分B級不動產、金融及服務業公司，定價尚未充分反映基本面；重點在於產業、評等與資本結構之內的個別差異。亞洲市場也可見這種分化：即使全球債券殖利率仍高，部分成熟借款人仍在爭取更低的信用加碼。

知情人士表示，聯想已啟動一筆$20億、5年期聯貸，條件為SOFR加75個基點，用於償還2022年同額借款；舊貸款定價為加碼110個基點，另有Libor轉換相關的信用調整利差。這次降低的是信用加碼，整體浮動利率利息支出是否下降仍未確定。

隨AI基礎建設擴張，聯想6月當季營收增加43%，並上調全年展望。銀行願意承作，也反映交易稀少：今年完成的中資離岸貸款只有54筆，為17年最低，總額卻升至$561億，主要受字節跳動$296億交易帶動。法國巴黎銀行、花旗、星展、匯豐及摩根大通共同統籌聯想這筆貸款。聯想股價本月已下跌約25%，但股價波動並未阻止其以更低貸款加碼向市場募資。

另據知情人士，美團取得中國監管許可後，正考慮未來幾週第二度發行離岸人民幣債券，資金將用於一般企業用途。人民幣融資成本較低，吸引借款人，今年點心債發行量已超過人民幣1兆元，美團可能加入這波發行。

Vestel管理層最新受訪內容，則在進行中的債務重整之外，補充了營運轉型計畫。執行長Gokhan Sigin表示，亞洲競爭持續，加上土耳其成本結構改變，公司必須轉向家電，並更有選擇地參與電視製造。公司在另行進行的銀行協商中，爭取本金與利息兩年寬限期，最終到期日為2041年；並希望在11月15日付息前完成國際債券交易。現有債券價格約為面額的25%。

Sigin提出削減固定成本、提升工廠效率、增加土耳其自有品牌銷售，以及拓展重型車充電與儲能業務。穆迪警告，暫時放寬的契約限制可能容許公司大幅增加債務，降低現有債權人的回收率。這種融資彈性與營運改革同時推進，而管理層認為，復甦必須仰賴後者。

## 英國通膨超預期，法債殖利率再觸關卡

英國9月消費者物價年增率由8月的3.1%升至3.5%，高於經濟學家預估的3.4%，並創11個月新高。車用燃料是主要推力，柴油價格在9月底創紀錄。服務通膨升至3.7%，商品價格漲幅則為2023年以來最快。

上游價格壓力也增強。生產者投入成本年增率由6.7%升至8.3%，製造商出廠售價上漲4.6%，為2023年4月以來最大升幅。機票、電玩與現場活動推升消費者物價，餐廳與旅館則是最大的向下抵銷項目。10月能源價格上限調整將進一步增加家庭能源帳單，英國央行預期2027年初通膨將超過4%。

施羅德經濟學家David Rees認為，成長具韌性，核心與服務通膨又上升，11月升息看來極有可能。RSM的Thomas Pugh則預期，能源、食品與記憶體晶片成本將進一步沿供應鏈傳導。週三上午交易時段，投資人維持對明年底前升息4次、每次25個基點的預期，第五次升息機率為60%。不過，當日稍晚的市場報導顯示，英國10年期公債殖利率反而下降3個基點至5.38%，德國10年期則上升2個基點至3.42%。

通膨也加重了財政負擔。英國公共債務首次超過£3兆，達GDP的94%。4至9月舉債£978億，較預算責任辦公室（OBR）3月預測高出£60億，即使本會計年度前5個月的舉債已向下修正£40億。9月單月舉債£245億，也高於預測及一年前水準。

稅收優於預期，支出增長卻更快，因通膨推高商品、服務、福利及利息成本。零售物價指數（RPI）通膨增加了通膨連結公債的支付金額，9月債務成本達£109億，創歷年同月紀錄，也高於OBR預估的£90億。全年債務利息支出如今超過£1,100億。

對財政大臣John Healey而言，新數據壓縮了10月28日預算案的選擇空間。4至9月經常預算口徑舉債£640億，超出預測£24億；中央政府淨投資£496億，比預測高£20億。政府承諾在2029至2030年度平衡日常支出與收入，現在不僅面臨更大的起始缺口，也承受協助民眾因應生活成本上升的要求。

法國10年期公債殖利率在週三歐洲交易時段上升7個基點，達5%，為2002年以來首次。相對德債的溢價擴大至159.4個基點，創15年最高；能源成本上揚之際，明年預算能否通過仍不確定。動盪也出現新的企業影響：家樂福下修全年獲利展望與其他目標，巴黎股價一度下跌15%。

道明的Pooja Kumra預期，接下來的預算表決將帶來壓力，而且即使通過，政治分裂與財政運作失靈仍會讓投資人不安。法債殖利率觸及新關卡時，歐洲天然氣期貨正上漲約4%，布蘭特原油在$110附近交易。法國融資溢價擴大，既反映與鄰國共同承受的能源衝擊，也反映自身財政調整難以落實。

ECB管理委員會委員Martins Kazaks表示，若通膨持續遠高於目標，可能仍需進一步緊縮，但他也強調，市場殖利率上升已帶來抑制作用。他向Econostream表示，經濟與勞動市場的強度不足以讓薪資要求再創高峰。持續通膨是他考慮進一步政策行動的條件，但市場自行收緊金融條件，也可能削弱成長與物價壓力。

首席經濟學家Philip Lane週三在上海談的則是國際貨幣使用對政策傳導的影響。他表示，歐元在國際間更廣泛使用，可透過歐元計價降低經濟對外部進口價格衝擊的敏感度，也可透過歐元融資成本，強化ECB政策對海外需求的影響。ECB已開始向全球大多數央行提供流動性取得管道。

## 亞洲央行分別運用匯率防守與內需支持工具

澳洲央行副總裁Andrew Hauser表示，通膨展望較8月預測惡化，顯著強化了再次升息的理由。AI與科技價格上升、資料中心建設熱潮及國內產能壓力，加上油價較央行假設高約三分之一，都在推升通膨。他也警告，部分企業開始把3%至3.5%的通膨視為常態，可能讓預期固化。

Bloomberg彙整的交換市場定價顯示，11月3日升息機率由談話前約30%升至約50%；市場完全反映一次25個基點升息的時間，也由5月提前至2月。澳幣上漲0.3%至70.26美分，3年期公債殖利率走高。Andrew Boak領導的高盛經濟學家團隊，將原先按兵不動的預測改為升息至4.85%，除非下週通膨數據弱於預期。

Hauser也承認勞動市場轉弱，使央行在抑制通膨時面臨取捨。澳洲央行今年已升息100個基點至4.6%。他的談話凸顯，下次決策須在保護就業與防止持續通膨根深蒂固之間權衡。

印尼央行選擇分別運用不同工具，維持BI-Rate在5.75%，符合38位受訪經濟學家中19位的預期，其餘半數原估升息。總裁Destry Damayanti同時宣布，12月前將銀行存款準備率調降2個百分點，釋出逾$100億供放貸，並將存款工具利率調高至5%，支持印尼盾資產報酬。

決策公布後，印尼盾貶至每美元18,005，10年期公債殖利率持平於7.44%，股市收復稍早失地，轉為上漲0.5%。Destry表示，央行正監控資金外流，穩定仍是首要目標。在基準指數重新分類仍有不確定性之際，這套組合旨在支持國內信用，同時避免削弱印尼盾存款的吸引力。

華僑銀行的Lavanya Venkateswaran認為，調降準備率是預防資金外流可能造成流動性緊縮。凱投宏觀的Jason Tuvey則較不認同，認為匯率支持與成長政策發出混雜訊號，可能削弱可信度，最終使利率更長時間維持高檔。央行指出，國內消費與財政刺激支撐穩健經濟，但外部展望較弱，面臨油價、通膨及成長低迷的挑戰。

印度的債務管理反應更為突然。印度央行拒絕原定規模INR2,300億的國庫券標售所有投標，為3月底以來首次全數取消，且未說明原因。Ujjivan Small Finance Bank的Rajeev Pawar認為，投標殖利率過高可能是原因，市場對央行進一步升息的預期正影響短端。

在此之前，印度公債遭拋售，10年期殖利率本月上升約24個基點，達2023年3月以來最高；5年期自9月底以來上升30個基點。流動性也趨緊：央行透過售債回收逾INR1兆，並進行大量外匯交換；銀行體系剩餘流動性由月初INR5兆，降至10月20日的INR5,700億。高油價與流動性變化，同時對主權融資施壓。

日本方面，Bloomberg最新調查顯示，經濟學家對政策正常化時點的預期明顯改變。83%預估12月18日將由目前1.25%升息，前次調查只有35%，當時最多人預測在1月行動。預期每隔3個月升息的比例，也由46%升至67%；終端利率預測中位數仍為1.75%。

前日本央行理事前田榮治另預測，12月將升息，接著在3月或4月再升。他認為政策利率最終可能需達2.25%，高於調查中位數，但警告若連續兩次會議升息，市場可能預期升息步調加快。日圓若急貶，可能使這種反應成為必要，不過他目前認為機率不高。

升息的國內影響，也反映在一筆房產出售案。知情人士表示，Kurosawa Group願意考慮以約¥800億出售銀座一棟大樓，低於最初¥1,200億的開價；該樓承租戶為Tiffany亞洲最大精品店。Tiffany的25年固定租金租約，使租金收入難以隨通膨與融資成本上升而調高。屋主沒有迫切現金壓力，仍可能保留物業。

經濟學家、前日本央行官員渡邊努週三另估計，通膨侵蝕既有債務實質價值，為日本帶來¥195兆利益，高於去年的¥180兆。這來自市場殖利率上升與約¥1,100兆既有公債實際付息利率調整之間的時間差。他將其界定為轉向2%通膨過程中的一次性利益，而非可持續支應經常支出的財源。

以色列在連續降息三次後，維持政策利率3.25%，符合16位受訪經濟學家的一致預期；央行預測12個月後利率為3%。央行將2026年成長預測由4%上調至5.6%，並預測2027年成長7.5%。但總裁Amir Yaron強調，以色列科技公司在海外生產，使用的本地勞動與資本不多，可能誇大國內經濟的強度。排除這項影響，今年與明年成長預測分別為3.4%與5.1%。這些預測假設低強度戰事與地緣政治緊張持續，且未納入下屆政府可能推出的財政立法。

## 財政選擇拉開主權與地方政府融資差距

南非中期預算削減每週發債規模，並推進財政錨，帶動債券上漲。10年期殖利率下降12個基點至8.84%，為逾一個月最低；截至約翰尼斯堡時間下午2時45分，南非幣扭轉稍早跌勢，升值0.1%至每美元16.37。Ninety One的Adam Furlan表示，發債削減幅度遠超預期，背後有較強稅收、融資組合調整與債券買回支撐。

財政部長Enoch Godongwana表示，債務已在2025至2026年度達GDP的78.4%高峰，此後將下降。截至3月的年度綜合財政赤字預估為3.9%，低於原估4%；初級盈餘預估為GDP的1.7%，高於2025至2026年度的1%。受礦業收入帶動，稅收預估將比2月估計高出ZAR171億，即使2026年成長預測由1.6%下修至1.2%。

政府已公布財政錨立法草案徵詢公眾意見，預計明年提交國會。草案採原則導向，要求每屆新政府在國會監督下訂定目標，使財政紀律朝長期制度要求邁進，同時讓歷屆政府自行設定具體目標。

融資計畫也將透過國內債券買回，平滑中期偏高的到期償還額，買回哪些到期年限將依市況決定。財政部估計，中期平均到期償還額為ZAR2,500億，並計畫動用ZAR110億現金餘額。外幣支付承諾意味著這段期間約需借款$155億，約每年$50億，且將優先取得優惠融資，再考慮發行國際債券。多邊貸款機構本會計年度已承諾提供$36億，其中$20億已撥付。

臨時燃油減負措施將減少ZAR100億收入，透過重新分配原撥給中央能源基金的資金支應。11月4日至12月1日，柴油與汽油稅費每公升分別減少ZAR3與ZAR1.50；之後至1月5日，改為較小的減幅，分別為ZAR1.50與ZAR1。財政部表示，未來干預措施必須維持財政中性。明確安排資金抵補，使政府得以提供減負措施而不放棄財政整頓目標。

阿根廷則因新的成長數據令人失望，債券走勢相反。週三稍早小漲的債券，在下午公布8月經濟活動意外年減1.7%後轉跌，加深市場對技術性衰退，以及明年選舉前總統Javier Milei改革方案能否維持政治支持的疑慮。本週稍早，主權債殖利率已接近12%。

融資限制包括明年約$250億硬通貨付款，其中1月Global與Bonar債券約需支付$45億。當地美元債銷售暫停，也關閉了一條原估今年可籌得額外$10億、明年$50億的管道。Global 2030債券的境內持有比例，由2024年底35.9%降至6月底23.3%；Global 2035債券居民持有比例則由35%降至19.5%。境外部位原已可觀，這些變化使市場更依賴外資承擔風險的意願。

Vontobel的Thierry Larose認為，價格反映的悲觀程度超過基本面所能解釋；VanEck的David Austerweil則強調對外部市場的依賴，以及2027年總統大選後政策延續的重要性。即使央行10月加快買入美元，新公布的經濟活動萎縮仍讓這場分歧更鮮明。週三整體硬通貨新興市場債利差小幅收窄，與阿根廷反轉走弱形成對照。

喀麥隆2033年到期美元債殖利率連升5天後超過11%，創1月發行以來最高，也高於評等較低的剛果同類債券。惠譽降評時提及，總統Paul Biya接班可能失序；他尚未任命依法可接任的副總統。在沒有IMF計畫、又愈來愈依賴外部資金的情況下，接班不確定性正直接增加融資困難。喀麥隆美元債10月已下跌約5%，同期較廣泛的新興市場美元債指標上漲0.6%。

巴西10月25日第二輪投票前，競選活動又帶來新的支出主張。Lula週三向國會提交方案，要求至少26.8%的國會預算修正撥款用於週末免費大眾運輸。政府估計年成本最高BRL120億，運輸業者協會估計則為BRL208億；他擴大大學生補助的提案，另需每年BRL46億。Flavio Bolsonaro陣營則承諾透過Pix退還部分能源與其他帳單支出，但未詳列成本。Bloomberg Economics的Adriana Dupita認為，若不加稅，這些承諾合計已超過可用財政空間。

美國地方政府也提出新的支出計畫，增加未來收入的負擔。芝加哥市長Brandon Johnson提議，授權發行$4.8億債券支付警察不當行為和解金，其中包括2027及2028年支付的$2.6億協議。他的$176億預算案希望填補營運基金$8.824億缺口，並透過雇主人頭稅、每件15美分包裹稅及提高雲端運算稅等措施，增加$6.642億收入。除每年逾$20億法定退休金支付外，另擬額外提撥$3.63億。市議會反對繼續舉債，加上可能遭降評，使預算通過更為複雜。

加州第38號提案將授權借款$84億用於免疫學研究，由一般基金償還，而非另增稅負。州議會分析辦公室估計，約20年間，每年本息支出為$5億至$6億。提案規定將研究發現收入的10%用於償債，但該辦公室表示，收入可能多年甚至數十年後才出現，且仍不確定。已承諾向擬設研究機構捐款$1.2億的Gary Michelson支持舉債；反對者Robert Kaplan估計，必須產生$1,200億智慧財產收益，才能收回這筆債券的成本。選民將於11月3日決定。

市政債基金流向顯示，投資人在賣壓期間轉換投資工具。LSEG Lipper記錄，截至10月14日當週，市政債ETF流入創紀錄的$50億，開放式基金卻流出$34億，為2022年6月以來最大單週贖回。經理人認為，部分資金轉移來自投資人實現虧損後，透過ETF重新進場。Capital Group的Mark Marinella表示，投資人並非放棄市政債；該資產10月至今已回升約2%。Municipal Market Analytics的Matt Fabian也預期，離開共同基金的資金，大部分仍會留在其他投資架構中。

## 後續市場觀察

房貸需求再度轉弱後，週四美國失業救濟金申請數據將提供下一個較全面的勞動市場檢驗。初領人數預估約20萬，續領人數預估172萬；9月領先指標預估下降0.1%。在短天期美債殖利率仍偏強之際，這些數據將協助判斷，房市已顯現的需求抑制是否正向外擴散。

10月22日的5年期TIPS標售，適逢10年期實質殖利率維持在2.75%附近、通膨補償上升。週五公布的10月標普全球PMI初值，將進一步擴大活動比較範圍：製造業共識預測55.5，前值55.9；服務業預估58，前值58.8。密西根大學通膨預期終值，一年期與五年期分別預估為4.7%與3.5%。在10月28日聯準會決策前，這些數據直接關係到利率敏感需求轉弱與價格預期持續偏高的平衡；市場共識預期聯準會維持4%利率不變。

日本週五通膨數據，整體年增率預估2.1%，排除生鮮食品及能源的指標預估2.3%，將供日本央行在10月30日評估基礎通膨。最新調查沒有經濟學家預期10月升息，但預測大幅轉向12月，加上委員可能意見不一，使措辭與投票結果都很重要。澳洲下週三公布第三季通膨，在Hauser示警與高盛調整預測後，將更直接牽動11月3日決策。

英國10月28日預算案，須在11月5日英國央行會議前，協調最新超支舉債、家庭減負與財政規則。法德利差升至159.4個基點後，法國接下來的預算表決仍是焦點。ECB將於10月29日開會，投資人壓倒性預期存款利率維持2.5%；Kazaks強調市場自行收緊金融條件，也為會前帶來政策上的考量。

能源仍能獨立改變這些判斷。Araghchi的條件使荷姆茲海峽重開，有賴談判促成美國政策改變；即使航運改善，煉油廠歲修仍可能延長油品供應吃緊。Anthropocene Fixed Income Institute本週新研究指出，在利率更高、債務更多的環境下，印尼、巴西與哥倫比亞尤其容易受到聖嬰現象干擾。糧食供給若受損，將在既有能源挑戰之外再添壓力。

AI融資下一個考驗，是營收成長能否同時支撐建設與可接受的新借款條件。Meta盤後財報將2026年資本支出展望區間下限調高，最新區間為$1,350億至$1,450億；特斯拉調整後獲利也超出預期。這些較晚公布的業績，將與SpaceX債券利差擴大、Nextdc供電延誤，以及DayOne重新考慮IPO的消息一起進入下一交易日。尚未解決的資金需求，如今須接受新營運數據與實際專案進度的檢驗，而不只是仰賴對AI長期需求的期待。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股回穩、美債曲線趨平，能源仍使通膨壓力難退
overall_summary.session_narrative:

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasury yields rose at shorter maturities on October 21 while the long bond extended its advance, leaving the curve flatter as renewed confidence in technology earnings met continuing inflation pressure. The two-year yield increased 2.99 basis points to 4.806%, the 10-year rose 1.05 basis points to 5.119%, and the 30-year declined 1.09 basis points to 5.4089%. Higher inflation compensation accounted for the small increase in the 10-year yield, with its real yield almost unchanged.

Technology shares recovered as SpaceX's results helped revive confidence in AI demand, but its bonds weakened as investors assessed the borrowing needed to finance that growth. That split gave the session its character: stronger operating results supported equities without settling how much new debt creditors would have to absorb. Oil added pressure from a different direction. Brent finished above $110 a barrel as attacks on shipping continued and Iran set conditions for renewed diplomacy.

Fresh mortgage figures showed that a small decline in U.S. borrowing costs had not revived housing demand. Overseas, Britain's inflation accelerated more than expected and its borrowing overshot forecasts, while French debt reached a new yield and spread milestone. South Africa supplied a contrasting fiscal result, rallying after a budget that reduced weekly bond issuance and advanced a new fiscal framework. These were distinct changes in financing conditions, rather than a synchronized response to the modest move in Treasuries.

## A Flatter Treasury Curve Meets Persistent Energy Pressure

The rise in short and intermediate Treasury yields accompanied a recovery in risk appetite during regular U.S. trading. The S&P 500 gained 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 advanced 1.13% and semiconductor shares rose 1.97%. SpaceX's earnings and strong preliminary figures from Super Micro Computer helped restore confidence in current technology demand after the recent reassessment of AI investment. The VIX declined 3.64% to 16.68.

Longer Treasuries nevertheless held up better than the front end. The five-year yield rose 2.15 basis points to 4.9506%, while the opposing moves at two and 30 years narrowed the 2s30s spread by 4.08 basis points to 60.29. The 2s10s spread contracted 1.94 basis points to 31.3. A recovery in technology shares therefore coincided with a further flattening, rather than a broad reversal of the recent long-duration rally.

The weekly comparisons show where that rally remained concentrated. Ten-year yields were 6.64 basis points lower over the week and 30-year yields down 11.42 basis points, against a 0.85-basis-point increase at two years. Over the month, however, the 10-year was still 12.2 basis points higher and the 30-year 8.19 basis points higher. The recent improvement at longer maturities had reduced, but not removed, the rise in financing costs.

At 10 years, the real yield slipped 0.09 basis point to 2.7494%, while breakeven inflation increased 1.14 basis points to 2.3696%. That left the nominal increase attributable to inflation compensation rather than renewed upward pressure on the real rate. Over the week, real yields had fallen 7.54 basis points even as breakevens rose 0.9 basis point. Inflation pricing continued to resist the improvement in longer government bonds.

Energy supplied a concrete reason for that resistance. Brent rose 1.16% to $110.05 a barrel, putting its weekly gain at 3.76% and its monthly advance at 10.84%. WTI finished at $98.05, up 0.24%. During the earlier session, an Iranian state-run outlet reported that a supertanker had struck a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz. Attacks on shipping continued to disrupt passage through the waterway.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran was prepared to negotiate an end to the war if Washington lifted its naval blockade and demonstrated a serious commitment to diplomacy. He also urged a return to the June Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, whose terms paired reopening the strait with ending the U.S. blockade, releasing frozen Iranian oil funds and removing sanctions. His proposal placed specific conditions on reopening talks while the shipping disruption remained active.

The U.S. inventory figures showed a larger draw in crude and gasoline than economists expected, but a build in distillates. EIA crude stocks fell 3.061 million barrels in the week ended October 16, compared with a 0.8 million-barrel decline expected and an 8.557 million draw previously. Gasoline inventories fell 2.952 million barrels against a 0.4 million decline expected, reversing the previous 3.518 million build. Distillate stocks increased 1.675 million barrels, against an expected 1.2 million draw and a previous decline of 2.527 million. The product detail was mixed even as crude and gasoline stocks tightened.

Morgan Stanley separately expects oil-product markets to remain tight through mid-2027, even if war-related disruption eases, because unusually heavy refinery maintenance will constrain supply. Goldman Sachs put global crude shipping costs at about seven times their level a year earlier. Those assessments concern the persistence and expense of physical supply, extending beyond the immediate diplomatic headlines.

U.S. housing provided a fresh indication of the restraint already coming from high rates. The Mortgage Bankers Association's 30-year fixed contract rate fell 9 basis points to 7.41% in the week ended October 16, its first decline since early August. Rates were still more than 1 percentage point above a year earlier. Purchase applications fell 7.3%, their seventh consecutive weekly decline, reaching the lowest level since early January 2025.

Total mortgage applications dropped 5.3%, following a 2.7% decline, and the mortgage market index fell to 188.6 from 199.2. The purchase index declined to 129.2 from 139.3. Refinancing weakened for a ninth consecutive week, with its index slipping to 503.1 from 513.5 and reaching its weakest level since the beginning of last year. The improvement in the mortgage rate was too small to arrest the deterioration in financing demand.

Treasury's 20-year bond auction cleared at 5.469%, compared with 5.420% at the previous sale. The higher auction yield added a realized long-maturity financing observation to a session in which the 30-year yield fell. The changing composition of demand for government debt is receiving increasing attention alongside those financing costs.

A Bloomberg examination published Wednesday put private investors' ownership at about 70% of federal debt, near its highest share since 1990. Hedge funds held roughly 8.5%, or $2.7 trillion, of outstanding Treasuries at the end of 2025, after quadrupling their positions between 2012 and 2025. Barclays strategist Anshul Pradhan argued that reliance on discretionary private capital can require larger price concessions than a market with substantial price-insensitive official demand.

Bloomberg Economics estimated that declining Fed and foreign official holdings had, at one point, added roughly 105 basis points of term premium. That is an estimate of the effect of a changing buyer base, not a measure of Wednesday's repricing. Corporate pensions also had about 114% of the assets needed to meet liabilities in September, according to Milliman, compared with 82% in July 2020. NISA's Stephen Douglass noted that frozen and closed defined-benefit plans stop accumulating new distant liabilities, limiting the growth of their long-term matching needs.

Leveraged buyers can absorb supply, but their funding conditions matter. TS Lombard's Steven Blitz said a sharp rise in repo rates could force relative-value positions to unwind. The same reporting noted that the Treasury basis trade had been shrinking in recent months. The new ownership analysis points to more discretionary demand without establishing a current funding-driven liquidation.

## AI Earnings Leave Creditors Focused on Funding

SpaceX's bonds fell Wednesday despite results that helped lift technology shares. The spread on its 6.6% notes due in 2046 widened 9 basis points to 264 basis points by 12:35 p.m. New York time. Five-year credit-default swaps rose as much as 0.8 basis point to about 232.6 basis points a year, reversing an earlier tightening, according to ICE Data Services.

The new focus was management's explanation of its investment plans. Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen said on Tuesday's earnings call that the company was investing aggressively in Super Intelligence computing, Starlink broadband and mobile services. He emphasized the intention to maintain investment-grade ratings while describing discussions with several pools of debt capital to fund growth. The current operating expansion was substantial: Super Intelligence revenue reached $7.56 billion in the September quarter, more than nine times its level a year earlier.

That combination explains the different equity and bond reactions. Higher revenue can strengthen the equity case for expansion while the financing of that expansion increases the supply creditors expect to absorb. SpaceX's existing discussions over $40 billion of chip financing form the immediate funding backdrop to Johnsen's new comments. The bond market's response centered on future capital requirements despite the earnings improvement.

Operational setbacks elsewhere showed how quickly expected project cash flows can change. Australia's Nextdc fell 42% Wednesday after cutting earnings guidance by more than a third and saying it was considering force majeure options. Community opposition had delayed power to a major Melbourne project. Singapore's DayOne Data Centers was considering delaying its U.S. IPO until markets recovered, or reducing the sale to $2.5 billion-$3 billion, roughly half its original ambition, according to people familiar with the plans.

Those developments concerned different stages of funding: Nextdc faced a delay in energizing an existing project, while DayOne was reconsidering the size and timing of an equity capital raise. Both matter to an industry whose construction spending precedes usable computing capacity. BlackRock Chief Executive Larry Fink offered a separate supply-side argument Wednesday, saying delays in building data centers could keep computing expensive and threaten growth, whereas faster construction could reduce those costs.

Apollo's Torsten Slok challenged the assumption of unlimited demand in a research note this week. A slowdown in spending on compute tokens suggested buyers were sensitive to even modest price changes and willing to reduce usage or find cheaper alternatives, he wrote. He also saw declining returns on capital squeezing data-center suppliers. His assessment put the economics of paid usage beside the funding and construction constraints facing providers.

The broader high-yield market was charging more for access even as U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly on Wednesday. Bloomberg's new aggregate tally put postponed U.S. and European debt sales above $5 billion this month across at least seven companies, the largest cluster of delays this year. U.S. junk-bond issuance was about $7 billion so far in October, compared with $51 billion in September. B-rated bond yields reached 8.39% Tuesday, an 18-month high, while CCC yields reached a four-year high of 15.7%.

The aggregate slowdown extends beyond the already troubled AI names. Circet postponed a EUR3 billion refinancing intended for the euro and dollar markets. ICG's David Saitowitz identified underlying rates as sufficient on their own to cool credit activity. Moody's John Puchalla likewise stressed the additional debt-service burden on highly leveraged borrowers. Wednesday's modest tightening in secondary high-yield spreads coexisted with a much more restrictive primary-market environment.

BlackRock's quarterly fixed-income outlook, released Wednesday, set out a different consequence of the rise in yields. It said a diversified portfolio could now yield more than 7% with duration below three years and an average rating of A-. James Turner, its head of global fixed income for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, emphasized that higher income provides greater resilience against rate increases or spread widening. Euro investment-grade corporate returns were down about 0.5% this year despite two ECB hikes and more than 20 basis points of widening from the tightest spreads, compared with a loss exceeding 13% in 2022.

The firm identified selected utility, telecom and energy corporate hybrids, and some B-rated real-estate, financial and service companies, as areas where pricing did not fully reflect fundamentals in its assessment. Its emphasis was on dispersion within sectors, ratings and capital structures. That distinction is visible in Asia, where some established borrowers are seeking lower credit margins even while global bond yields remain elevated.

Lenovo launched syndication of a $2 billion five-year loan at 75 basis points over SOFR, according to people familiar with the transaction. The facility is intended to refinance an equal-sized 2022 borrowing priced at 110 basis points plus a credit adjustment spread associated with the transition from Libor. The narrower margin concerns the credit component of borrowing, rather than establishing a reduction in the entire floating-rate interest bill.

Lenovo's revenue increased 43% in the June quarter and it raised its fiscal-year outlook as AI infrastructure expanded. Banks' appetite also reflects a shortage of deals: only 54 offshore Chinese loans had completed this year, a 17-year low, although their combined value rose to $56.1 billion, largely because of ByteDance's $29.6 billion transaction. BNP Paribas, Citi, DBS, HSBC and JPMorgan are coordinating Lenovo's facility. Its shares had fallen about 25% this month, illustrating that equity volatility had not prevented it from marketing tighter loan terms.

Meituan was considering its second offshore yuan bond offering in coming weeks after receiving Chinese regulatory permission, according to people familiar with the matter. Proceeds would be for general corporate purposes. The potential sale joins a dim sum market where issuance has exceeded CNY1 trillion this year as lower yuan financing costs attract borrowers.

Vestel's fresh management interview added a business overhaul to its pending debt restructuring. Chief Executive Gokhan Sigin said persistent Asian competition and Turkey's changed cost structure required a shift toward household appliances and more selective participation in television manufacturing. The company is seeking a two-year grace period on principal and interest in separate bank negotiations, with final maturity in 2041, and aims to complete its Eurobond deal before the November 15 coupon. Existing notes traded around 25 cents on the dollar.

Sigin described fixed-cost reductions, factory-efficiency improvements, greater own-brand sales in Turkey and expansion into heavy-vehicle charging and energy storage. Moody's warned that temporarily relaxed covenants could permit substantial new debt and reduce existing creditors' recoveries. That financing flexibility sits alongside the operating changes on which management says recovery must depend.

## Britain's Inflation Surprise and France's New Yield Milestone

British consumer inflation accelerated to 3.5% year on year in September from 3.1% in August, exceeding economists' 3.4% forecast and reaching an 11-month high. Motor fuel was the principal driver, with diesel prices reaching a record in late September. Services inflation increased to 3.7%, while goods prices rose at their fastest pace since 2023.

The pipeline figures also strengthened. Producer input costs increased 8.3% year on year, up from 6.7%, and manufacturers' selling prices rose 4.6%, their largest increase since April 2023. Airfares, computer games and live events contributed to consumer-price acceleration, while restaurants and hotels provided the largest downward drag. Household energy bills face a further increase from the October price cap, and the Bank of England expects inflation to exceed 4% in early 2027.

Schroders economist David Rees said resilient growth and rising core and services inflation made a November increase look highly likely. RSM's Thomas Pugh expected further energy, food and memory-chip costs to pass through supply chains. During Wednesday morning trading, investors maintained expectations for four quarter-point increases by the end of next year, with a 60% probability of a fifth. The day's later market account nevertheless put the 10-year gilt yield 3 basis points lower at 5.38%, while Germany's rose 2 basis points to 3.42%.

The fiscal release complicated the same inflation problem. British public debt exceeded GBP3 trillion for the first time, reaching 94% of GDP. April-September borrowing was GBP97.8 billion, GBP6 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility's March projection, despite a GBP4 billion downward revision to borrowing in the first five months of the fiscal year. September alone recorded GBP24.5 billion of borrowing, above both the forecast and the year-earlier result.

Tax receipts were stronger than expected, but spending increased faster as inflation lifted the cost of goods, services, welfare and interest. September debt costs reached GBP10.9 billion, a record for that month and above the OBR's GBP9 billion forecast, as RPI inflation increased payments on index-linked gilts. Annual debt service now exceeds GBP110 billion.

For Chancellor John Healey, the new figures narrow the choices before the October 28 budget. Borrowing on the current-budget measure was GBP64 billion in April-September, GBP2.4 billion above forecast, while central-government net investment reached GBP49.6 billion, GBP2 billion above projection. The commitment to balance day-to-day spending and revenue by 2029-30 now faces a larger starting shortfall alongside demands for relief from rising living costs.

French 10-year yields reached 5% for the first time since 2002, rising 7 basis points during Wednesday's European trading. The premium over Germany widened to 159.4 basis points, the largest in 15 years. Higher energy costs combined with continued uncertainty over passage of next year's budget. Carrefour supplied a new corporate consequence of the unrest, cutting its annual profit outlook and other targets and falling as much as 15% in Paris.

TD's Pooja Kumra expected pressure around upcoming budget votes and argued that passage alone would leave investors concerned about political fragmentation and fiscal dysfunction. The new yield milestone came while European gas futures were rising around 4% and Brent was trading near $110. France's widening financing penalty therefore combined an energy shock shared with neighbors and continuing difficulty delivering its own fiscal adjustment.

ECB Governing Council member Martins Kazaks said further tightening might be needed if inflation remained far above target, but highlighted the restraint already coming from higher market yields. He told Econostream that the economy and labor market were not strong enough to push wage demands to new heights. His condition for more policy action was persistent inflation, tempered by market-driven tightening that could weaken growth and price pressure.

Chief Economist Philip Lane addressed a different policy channel in Shanghai Wednesday. Greater international use of the euro could reduce sensitivity to external import-price shocks through euro invoicing, he said, and strengthen the effect of ECB policy on foreign demand through euro funding costs. The ECB has begun offering liquidity access to most central banks worldwide. Lane's argument concerned the transmission benefits of international currency use rather than a change in the immediate rate outlook.

## Asian Policymakers Separate Currency Defense From Demand Support

Australia's Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser materially strengthened the case for another RBA increase, saying the inflation outlook had worsened since the August forecast. Higher AI and technology prices, a data-center construction boom and domestic capacity pressure were adding to an oil price roughly a third above the bank's assumption. He also warned that some firms were starting to treat 3%-3.5% inflation as normal, creating a risk that expectations became entrenched.

Swaps pricing compiled by Bloomberg moved the probability of a November 3 increase to about 50% from roughly 30% before his remarks. A quarter-point rise was fully priced by February rather than May. The Australian dollar rose 0.3% to 70.26 U.S. cents and three-year government yields increased. Goldman Sachs economists led by Andrew Boak changed their forecast from a hold to a rise taking the cash rate to 4.85%, unless next week's inflation figures proved weaker than expected.

Hauser acknowledged the weakening labor market, preserving a genuine counterweight to the inflation message. The RBA has already tightened 100 basis points this year, taking its rate to 4.6%. His comments framed the next decision as a choice between protecting employment and allowing persistent inflation to become embedded, rather than dismissing the recent labor deterioration.

Bank Indonesia chose to separate its instruments. It held the BI-Rate at 5.75%, matching 19 of 38 economists while the other half expected an increase. Governor Destry Damayanti paired that decision with a 2-percentage-point reduction in bank reserve requirements by December, releasing more than $10 billion for lending, and an increase in the deposit facility rate to 5% to support returns on rupiah assets.

The rupiah slipped to 18,005 per dollar after the announcement, while the 10-year government yield was steady at 7.44% and stocks recovered earlier losses to trade 0.5% higher. Destry said stability remained the priority as the bank monitored capital outflows. The combination sought to support domestic credit without reducing the attraction of rupiah deposits amid the continuing benchmark-reclassification uncertainty.

OCBC's Lavanya Venkateswaran saw the reserve reduction as a preemptive response to potentially tighter liquidity from outflows. Capital Economics' Jason Tuvey was less convinced, arguing that mixed signals over currency support and growth could weaken credibility and ultimately keep rates high for longer. The central bank described domestic consumption and fiscal stimulus as supporting a solid economy, against a weaker external outlook marked by oil costs, inflation and subdued growth.

India's debt-management response was more abrupt. The RBI rejected every bid at a planned INR230 billion Treasury-bill sale, the first complete cancellation since late March, without explaining its reason. Ujjivan Small Finance Bank's Rajeev Pawar considered excessively high offered yields a probable explanation and said expectations of further RBI increases were affecting short maturities.

The cancellation followed a selloff that had lifted 10-year yields about 24 basis points this month to their highest since March 2023. Five-year yields were up 30 basis points since September's end. Liquidity had also tightened: the RBI drained more than INR1 trillion through bond sales and conducted substantial foreign-exchange swaps, while the banking surplus fell to INR570 billion on October 20 from INR5 trillion at the beginning of the month. Elevated oil and changing liquidity conditions were both pressing on sovereign financing.

In Japan, a new Bloomberg survey showed a substantial change in the expected timing of normalization. Some 83% of economists expected a December 18 hike from the current 1.25%, against 35% in the previous survey, when January had been the most popular choice. The share expecting increases every three months rose to 67% from 46%. The median terminal-rate forecast remained 1.75%.

Former BOJ executive director Eiji Maeda separately forecast increases in December and then March or April. He thought the policy rate might eventually need to reach 2.25%, above the survey median, but warned that consecutive-meeting increases could cause markets to anticipate an accelerating sequence. A sharp yen depreciation could make such a response necessary, although he did not see it as likely now.

The domestic consequences of higher rates were visible in a property offering. Kurosawa Group was prepared to consider about JPY80 billion for the Ginza building housing Tiffany's largest Asian boutique, down from an initial JPY120 billion asking price, according to people familiar with the matter. Tiffany's 25-year fixed-rent lease limits the ability to raise income as inflation and financing costs increase. The owner is not under urgent cash pressure and may still retain the property.

Economist and former BOJ official Tsutomu Watanabe offered a separate estimate of the fiscal effect of inflation Wednesday. He put Japan's gain from the erosion of outstanding debt's real value at JPY195 trillion, up from JPY180 trillion last year. The gain reflects the delay between rising market yields and the rates paid on roughly JPY1,100 trillion of existing government debt. He characterized it as a one-time benefit from the transition to 2% inflation, distinct from sustainable funding for continuing expenditure.

Israel held its policy rate at 3.25%, unanimously expected by 16 surveyed economists, after three successive cuts. Its projected rate 12 months ahead was 3%. The bank raised 2026 growth to 5.6% from 4% and forecast 7.5% for 2027, but Governor Amir Yaron stressed that production abroad by Israeli technology firms could exaggerate the strength of domestic activity because it uses little local labor or capital. Excluding that effect, growth was projected at 3.4% this year and 5.1% next year. The forecasts assume low-intensity fighting and continued geopolitical tension, and exclude potential fiscal legislation by the next government.

## Fiscal Decisions Divide Sovereigns and Municipal Borrowers

South African bonds rallied after the medium-term budget combined lower weekly issuance with progress toward a fiscal anchor. The 10-year yield fell 12 basis points to 8.84%, its lowest in more than a month, while the rand reversed an earlier loss to trade 0.1% stronger at 16.37 per dollar by 2:45 p.m. Johannesburg time. Ninety One's Adam Furlan said the issuance reduction was much larger than expected, supported by stronger revenue, a changed financing mix and buybacks.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said debt had peaked at 78.4% of GDP in 2025-26 and would decline thereafter. The consolidated deficit was projected at 3.9% in the year through March, against 4% previously, and the primary surplus at 1.7% of GDP, up from 1% in 2025-26. Tax revenue was projected to exceed February's estimate by ZAR17.1 billion, helped by mining receipts, even as the 2026 growth forecast was lowered to 1.2% from 1.6%.

The government released draft fiscal-anchor legislation for public comment, with parliamentary introduction expected next year. Its principles-based approach would require each new administration to specify targets under parliamentary oversight. The framework moves fiscal discipline toward an enduring institutional requirement while leaving targets to successive governments.

The financing plan also provides for domestic buybacks to smooth elevated medium-term redemptions, with target maturities determined by market conditions. Treasury put average redemptions at ZAR250 billion over the medium term and planned a ZAR11 billion drawdown in cash balances. Foreign-currency commitments imply about $15.5 billion of borrowing over that horizon, or roughly $5 billion annually, with concessional finance prioritized before eurobond issuance. Multilateral lenders had already committed $3.6 billion this fiscal year, of which $2 billion had been disbursed.

Temporary fuel relief will cost ZAR10 billion in forgone revenue, financed by reallocating money transferred to the Central Energy Fund. Diesel levies will fall ZAR3 a liter and gasoline levies ZAR1.50 from November 4 to December 1; smaller reductions of ZAR1.50 and ZAR1 will continue until January 5. Treasury said future interventions must be fiscally neutral. The specified funding offsets allow relief without abandoning the budget's consolidation objective.

Argentina's bonds moved in the opposite direction after a fresh growth disappointment. Securities that had gained modestly earlier Wednesday reversed in the afternoon when August economic activity fell an unexpected 1.7% year on year. The result increased concern about a technical recession and the durability of political support for President Javier Milei's program ahead of next year's election. Sovereign yields had approached 12% earlier in the week.

The financing constraint includes roughly $25 billion of hard-currency payments next year, with about $4.5 billion due in January on Global and Bonar bonds. Suspended local dollar-bond sales closed a channel expected to raise another $1 billion this year and $5 billion next year. Domestic ownership of Global 2030 bonds fell to 23.3% at June's end from 35.9% at the end of 2024; the resident share of Global 2035 notes declined to 19.5% from 35%. Those changes leave a market with substantial offshore positions more dependent on foreign investors' willingness to hold risk.

Vontobel's Thierry Larose argued that prices reflected more pessimism than fundamentals justified. VanEck's David Austerweil instead emphasized dependence on external markets and the importance of policy continuity after the 2027 presidential election. The new activity contraction sharpened that disagreement despite the central bank's accelerated October dollar purchases. Broad hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly Wednesday, contrasting with Argentina's reversal.

Cameroon's 2033 dollar yield exceeded 11%, its highest since issuance in January, after five days of increases. It moved above comparable debt from lower-rated Congo. Fitch's downgrade cited the risk of a disorderly succession to President Paul Biya, who has not appointed the vice-president legally positioned to succeed him. With no IMF program and increasing dependence on external funding, succession uncertainty is directly complicating financing. Its dollar debt had lost about 5% in October against a 0.6% gain in a broader emerging-market dollar-bond gauge.

Brazil's campaign added fresh spending proposals before the October 25 runoff. Lula sent Congress a plan Wednesday requiring at least 26.8% of congressional budget amendments to fund free weekend public transport. The government estimated an annual cost up to BRL12 billion, while the transport companies' association put it at BRL20.8 billion. His expanded university aid proposal would cost BRL4.6 billion annually. Flavio Bolsonaro's campaign separately promised cash back on energy and other bills through Pix without detailing its cost. Bloomberg Economics' Adriana Dupita argued that the combined promises exceeded available fiscal space without additional taxes.

U.S. municipal borrowers also put new claims on future revenue. Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson proposed $480 million of bond authorization for police-misconduct settlements, including a $260 million agreement payable in 2027 and 2028. His $17.6 billion budget seeks to close an $882.4 million operating-fund gap and raise an additional $664.2 million through measures including an employer head tax, a 15-cent package levy and a higher cloud-computing tax. A $363 million supplemental pension contribution would come on top of more than $2 billion in required annual payments. Council resistance to further debt and possible rating cuts complicates approval.

California's Proposition 38 would authorize $8.4 billion for immunology research, repaid from the general fund rather than a new tax. The Legislative Analyst's Office estimates annual debt service of $500 million-$600 million for about 20 years. The measure assigns 10% of discovery revenue to repayment, but the agency says proceeds could take years or decades and remain uncertain. Gary Michelson, who has pledged $120 million to the proposed institute, supports the borrowing; critic Robert Kaplan estimates recouping the bond's costs would require $120 billion of intellectual property. Voters decide November 3.

Municipal fund flows showed investors changing vehicles during the selloff. LSEG Lipper recorded a record $5 billion entering muni ETFs in the week ended October 14, while open-ended funds lost $3.4 billion, their largest weekly withdrawal since June 2022. Managers attributed part of the switch to investors realizing losses and reentering through ETFs. Capital Group's Mark Marinella said investors were not abandoning the asset class, which had recovered about 2% so far in October. Municipal Market Analytics' Matt Fabian expected much of the money leaving mutual funds to remain in other structures.

## Forward Market Significance

Thursday's U.S. claims releases provide the next broad labor test after mortgage demand weakened again. Initial claims are expected around 200,000 and continuing claims at 1.720 million. The September leading index is expected to decline 0.1%. Together they will help establish whether the restraint visible in housing is spreading while short Treasury yields remain firm.

The October 22 five-year TIPS auction arrives with 10-year real yields holding near 2.75% and inflation compensation rising. Friday's preliminary October S&P Global PMIs then broaden the activity comparison: manufacturing consensus is 55.5 after 55.9, and services 58 after 58.8. Final Michigan inflation expectations are expected at 4.7% over one year and 3.5% over five years. Those releases bear directly on the balance between weakening rate-sensitive demand and persistent price expectations before the October 28 Fed decision, for which consensus expects an unchanged 4% rate.

Japan's Friday inflation figures are expected to put headline inflation at 2.1% and the measure excluding fresh food and energy at 2.3%. The distinction matters before the October 30 BOJ assessment of underlying inflation. No economist in the new survey expects an October increase, but the sharp shift toward December and possible disagreement among board members leave the language and vote important. Australia's Q3 inflation release next Wednesday is more immediately tied to the November 3 decision after Hauser's warning and Goldman's revised forecast.

Britain's October 28 budget must reconcile the new borrowing overshoot with household relief and the fiscal rules before the November 5 BOE meeting. France's pending budget votes remain central after the spread reached 159.4 basis points. Kazaks' emphasis on market-driven restraint adds a policy question before the ECB's October 29 meeting, where investors overwhelmingly expect the deposit rate to remain 2.5%.

Energy retains an independent capacity to change those assessments. Araghchi's conditions leave the reopening of Hormuz tied to a negotiated change in U.S. policy, while product-market maintenance could prolong tightness even if shipping improves. New research this week by the Anthropocene Fixed Income Institute identified Indonesia, Brazil and Colombia as particularly vulnerable to El Niño disruption in a higher-rate, higher-debt environment. Food-supply damage would add to the existing energy challenge; it is a separate prospective pressure rather than an explanation for Wednesday's small Treasury move.

AI financing faces its next test in whether stronger revenue can support both construction and acceptable new borrowing terms. Meta's after-hours earnings announcement lifted the low end of its 2026 capital-spending outlook to a range of $135 billion-$145 billion, and Tesla's adjusted earnings exceeded expectations. Those later results enter the next session alongside SpaceX's widening bond spread, Nextdc's power delay and DayOne's reconsidered IPO. The unresolved financing requirement is now being tested against fresh operating figures and actual project execution, not simply expectations of long-run AI demand.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Shorter Treasury yields rose while the long bond extended its advance: the 2-year increased 2.99 basis points to 4.806%, the 10-year rose 1.05 basis points to 5.119%, and the 30-year fell 1.09 basis points to 5.4089%. The 10-year real yield slipped 0.09 basis point as breakeven inflation rose 1.14 basis points, leaving inflation compensation responsible for the nominal increase.

SpaceX's results helped revive confidence in AI demand, but its bonds weakened as management discussed debt capital to finance expansion. Stronger earnings did not settle the financing burden on creditors. Brent finished above $110 a barrel amid continuing attacks on shipping, while Iran conditioned renewed negotiations on changes in U.S. policy. Mortgage purchase applications fell for a seventh consecutive week despite a small decline in borrowing costs.

Overseas financing conditions diverged. British inflation accelerated to 3.5% and borrowing exceeded forecasts; French 10-year yields reached 5% during European trading, with the premium over Germany widening to 159.4 basis points. South African bonds instead rallied after a budget that cut weekly issuance and advanced a fiscal anchor. The next U.S. labor and inflation-expectations releases will test whether weakening rate-sensitive demand is spreading while price pressure persists.
